title: Shoot first and be condemned later
article: It is common knowledge: a person runs the risk of being shot by RCMP if he or she is in possession of a firearm (or anything that resembles one) in a standoff with police.

Although it is early in the investigation into the Feb. 10th tragedy in 100 Mile House when Shelley Richards was shot, allegedly by her common-law husband Gordon Wilson. Wilson was then confronted and shot by a still unnamed officer in front of a neighbour's home. The internet reaction has been swift and brutal toward RCMP.

The officer involved has been instantly condemned in some people's minds, comparing the incident to the Robert Dziekanski Tasering incident and the more recent charging of two police Lower Mainland officers for beating a delivery man.
If the 100 Mile man really did confront RCMP with a shotgun, the outcome of the incident should come as no surprise.
Who do these same people call when they run into trouble? Superman?
Life is no comic book; citizens rely on police enforcement when they encounter problems.
All around this is a horribly sad situation: two people lost their lives and the officer, forced to make such a heavy decision, is left with a world of what ifs.
And it's interesting: the anti-Taser advocates fall silent on this issue; now the net is full of comments about how the officer should have used a Taser and not a gun.
Yes, there are some acts by the human beings paid to protect residents that are irreprehensible.
Human beings, inherently, will make mistakes. And some humans are not good to begin with. But that does not mean that every priest is a molester, every activist is a terrorist or every cop a killer.
Why are people so quick to judge a lawman?
What if an officer or a bystander had been shot and killed, instead of the alleged suspect?

With a disturbing increase in gun violence all over the province, more officers may have to make the hardest decision a cop probably ever has to make: do I shoot or do I ask him to put the gun down one more time, which risks my life and the lives of those around me?
Are there so many rogue "cowboy" cops that the public assume the cop is guilty before the suspect (which should be wrong on both accounts)?
People are never happy; cops are crucified when they use any sort of force, whether baton, Taser or gun. Just wait for the facts before hammering in the final nail.
